 Want Caribbean sun without a passport? Try these 4 islands for a winter getaway
 You don't need a passport to plan a Caribbean beach trip. These islands offer an easier way for U.S. travelers to enjoy turquoise water without international travel hurdles.
 Adrienne Barile   Creator of The Haphazard Traveler • Follow Updated Oct 22, 2026 Updated Thu, October 22, 2026 at 10:20 AM UTC 6 min read Aerial view of Caneel Bay and the North Shore of St. John, United States Virgin Islands (cdwheatley via Getty Images) If you don't have a current passport or simply don't want the extra hassle of international travel, you can still plan a Caribbean beach trip this fall or winter.
 For U.S. citizens, there are islands where you can fly, laze on a beach, and swim in warm waters without a passport, because they're part of the United States. Think: Caribbean vibes, domestic flight.
 Here are four island picks to start with, plus what each one does best.
 Advertisement Advertisement Quick note: all of this applies to U.S. citizens and permanent residents. Visitors from other countries still need to follow the same passport/visa requirements you'd use to enter the mainland U.S.
 Puerto Rico: Beaches, culture, and an "easy" Caribbean trip
 Castillo San Felipe del Morro has guarded the entrance to San Juan Bay for more than 400 years. It's one of Puerto Rico's most iconic landmarks and an easy walk from Old San Juan's restaurants, shops, and colorful streets.
 If you want to step off the plane and immediately feel like you've gone somewhere different, Puerto Rico is one of the easiest Caribbean getaways for U.S. travelers. As a U.S. territory, U.S. citizens can fly there with a REAL ID-compliant driver's license or other accepted identification—no passport, customs line, or currency exchange required. Most visitors arrive through Luis Muñoz Marín International Airport (SJU) in San Juan.
 Puerto Rico offers an easy mix of beach time, history, and outdoor adventure. Spend a few days exploring Old San Juan's colorful streets, cafés, and Spanish forts before relaxing on nearby beaches like Condado or Isla Verde. If you have more time, head east to explore El Yunque National Forest, kayak a bioluminescent bay, or take a ferry or short flight to Vieques or Culebra, where Flamenco Beach is regularly ranked among the world's best.
 Puerto Rico is a great choice if you want more than a beach vacation. Between its historic sites, food scene, rainforests, and beautiful coastline, it's easy to combine sightseeing and relaxation without ever feeling like you've spent your entire trip at a resort.
 St. Thomas, U.S. Virgin Islands: Easy beaches, boating, and resort stays
 Regularly ranked among the Caribbean's best beaches, Magens Bay is known for its calm, sheltered water, making it a favorite for swimming, paddleboarding, and families.
 St. Thomas is one of the easiest Caribbean islands for U.S. travelers to visit. As part of the U.S. Virgin Islands, U.S. citizens can fly here into St. Thomas ( airport code STT )from the mainland with a government-issued ID instead of a passport.
 Advertisement Advertisement The island combines beautiful beaches with the convenience of a well-developed tourism infrastructure. Visitors can choose from beachfront resorts, boutique hotels, and vacation rentals, while day trips by boat make it easy to explore nearby cays and snorkel reefs.
 Spend your days relaxing at beaches like Magens Bay, Sapphire Beach, or Coki Beach, book a catamaran cruise or snorkeling excursion, or browse the shops and restaurants in Charlotte Amalie. You can enjoy a classic Caribbean vacation without needing to rent a car or coordinate multiple ferries.
 Before you return home: U.S. citizens flying back to the mainland don't need a passport, but it's a good idea to travel with a REAL ID-compliant driver's license or other government-issued photo ID and another document proving U.S. citizenship, such as a birth certificate, in case it's requested.
 St. John, U.S. Virgin Islands: National park beaches and a quieter island escape
 Trunk Bay is famous for its underwater snorkeling trail, where interpretive signs beneath the surface introduce visitors to coral reefs and marine life.
 Just a short ferry ride from St. Thomas, St. John offers a very different Caribbean experience. Nearly two-thirds of the island is protected as Virgin Islands National Park , helping preserve its forests, hiking trails, historic sugar plantation ruins, and some of the Caribbean's most beautiful beaches.
 Advertisement Advertisement Rather than large resorts, you'll find smaller hotels, vacation villas, and the relaxed waterfront community of Cruz Bay. From there, it's easy to explore famous beaches such as Trunk Bay, Cinnamon Bay, and Maho Bay, where calm, clear water makes snorkeling accessible for many visitors.
 St. John is a great choice if your ideal vacation includes mornings on scenic hiking trails, afternoons snorkeling or swimming, and evenings enjoying casual restaurants overlooking the harbor. It feels quieter and more connected to nature than neighboring St. Thomas while remaining easy to combine with the larger island on the same trip.
 Before you return home: U.S. citizens flying back to the mainland don't need a passport, but it's a good idea to travel with a REAL ID-compliant driver's license or other government-issued photo ID and another document proving U.S. citizenship, such as a birth certificate, in case it's requested.
 Just offshore from St. Croix, Buck Island Reef National Monument protects one of the Caribbean's best-preserved coral reef systems and is best explored on a guided snorkeling or sailing excursion.
 St. Croix, U.S. Virgin Islands: History, reefs, and a slower island pace
 If you're looking for a quieter Caribbean vacation, St. Croix offers a more relaxed alternative to St. Thomas. As the largest of the U.S. Virgin Islands, it combines historic towns, excellent snorkeling and diving, and scenic drives without the crowds found on some of the region's busier islands.
 Advertisement Advertisement Visitors can explore the colorful streets of Christiansted , stroll its waterfront boardwalk, or take a boat trip to Buck Island Reef National Monument , home to one of the Caribbean's most celebrated underwater snorkeling trails. On the island's west end, Frederiksted has a slower pace, with a historic waterfront and a pier that's popular for diving and snorkeling.
 St. Croix is a great choice if you prefer a vacation that's less about hopping from one attraction to the next and more about settling into island life. Spend your mornings snorkeling or exploring historic sites, enjoy a leisurely lunch overlooking the water, then end the day watching the sunset from a quiet beach.
 Before you return home: As with St. Thomas and St. John, U.S. citizens don't need a passport to fly back to the mainland, but it's a good idea to travel with a REAL ID-compliant driver's license or other government-issued photo ID and another document proving U.S. citizenship, such as a birth certificate, in case it's requested.
 A few practical notes before you book
 ID & REAL ID: For U.S. citizens, travel to Puerto Rico and the USVI is treated like domestic air travel. A REAL ID–compliant license or other accepted ID is usually enough, but check current TSA/REAL ID rules before you go.
 Non-U.S. citizens: You'll need the same passport/visa you'd use to enter the mainland U.S. These islands aren't a workaround for international travel rules.
 Hurricane season: Officially June–November. Lots of people still travel then, but if you want to lower your storm risk, aim for December–April.
 Advertisement Advertisement If your passport is in limbo or you just don't feel like dealing with international travel this year, you don't have to give up on clear water and palm trees.
 Pick Puerto Rico for a mix of city and beach , St. Thomas + St. John for easy resort-plus-boat-days, or St. Croix for a slower , reef-forward escape, then treat it like what it is: a Caribbean vacation that just happens to be as simple as flying somewhere else in the U.S.
 If this sent you checking flights to the Caribbean when you were just trying to be responsible, my work here is done. Follow me below on Yahoo for more travel ideas, and find me on Instagram at @thehaphazardtraveler for real-time adventures.
